trust_decision.summary: Whether oct key material may be empty is decided at key-material entry (OctKey.import_key over the OctBinding deserializer) and again immediately before hmac.new in HMACAlgorithm.sign/verify; at the pinned commit neither place rejects b"", so HS256/HS384/HS512 sign and verify accept the empty key and produce a digest any party can reproduce.

landing_point.why: The summary names HS256/HS384/HS512 verify; HMACAlgorithm.verify is the only HS verify implementation and it feeds key.get_op_key("verify") straight into hmac.new with no emptiness check.

fix_sites.entry_point: jwa.HMACAlgorithm.sign / jwa.HMACAlgorithm.verify, reached by jws.serialize_compact, jws.deserialize_compact, jws.serialize_json, jws.deserialize_json, jwt.encode and jwt.decode
fix_sites.module_kind: JWS algorithm implementation (JWA plugin; low-level public algorithm API)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: OctKey.import_key is the generic key-import/JWK-reload API, not the HS* code path the report names, and it already deliberately only warns for short keys, so rejecting empty material there reads as an unrelated API change the report never asked for.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-empty but short keys must keep being accepted with only a SecurityWarning (the 112-bit size is advisory here); the suite relies on 3- and 6-byte secrets such as b"rfc" and "secret", so a fix that enforces the 14-byte minimum or the hash-output length instead of emptiness breaks every JWS/JWT fixture.

O6_input_shapes: OctKey whose raw_value is set to b"" after construction (programmatic empty key)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OctKey.generate_key(0) / jwk.generate_key("oct", 0) builds b"" via secrets.token_bytes(0) and calls the constructor directly, so the new non-empty rule at OctKey.import_key never runs on this key-material route.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Key generation is not key import; a 0-bit key is caller error, and the HMAC-layer guard already stops it from being used for HS* verification.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The public OctKey(b"", b"", ...) constructor stores an empty raw_value (BaseKey.__init__ has no check); the published fix only re-guards the JWS HMAC sink, so PBES2-HS256/384/512 still feeds that empty key to PBKDF2-HMAC as the password (jwe_algs.py:290,304).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The public constructor is a low-level API and the fix's own comment treats direct construction as expected; PBES2 is JWE password-based key management, not the HS* verification named in the report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one subpackage boundary (_rfc7517 vs _rfc7518) plus the JWE alg module

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an explicit non-empty validation (or rejection of key_size == 0) in OctKey.generate_key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix already owns this file and chose the import path; a maintainer hardening "empty oct key material" would plausibly cover the sibling generation path too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an empty-hkey guard in CBCHS2EncModel._hmac, the library's only other hmac.new call site
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the second HMAC construction in the tree; a maintainer repeating the "HMAC key must not be empty" defence-in-depth would naturally add the same check there.
PBES2 already treats an OctKey as a password, so a maintainer reviewing empty key material across the JOSE algorithms could guard the password-based route next.

O9_family: improper authentication via empty/weak HMAC key material (CWE-287, CWE-1391, CWE-326)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools build (pyproject.toml:42-44), pip, pytest with pythonpath=src; runtime dependency cryptography>=45.0.1 (pyproject.toml:5-7)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/jws/test_compact.py, tests/jws/test_json.py, tests/jws/test_rfc7797.py, tests/jws/test_errors.py, tests/jwk/test_oct_key.py, tests/jwk/test_key_methods.py, tests/jwt/*; plain unittest TestCase run under pytest (pyproject.toml:79-88).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Patch only HMACAlgorithm.verify (the path the report names) with a truthiness check, leaving sign, OctKey.import_key and the JWK-dict / generate_key routes untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: JWE decrypt silently replaces a CEK whose length mismatches enc.cek_size with a random CEK (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/message.py:124-125) instead of raising; noticed but not pursued as it is a separate behaviour.
